newsitem.title: CHINA: China car imports seen falling to low in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China car imports seen falling to low in 1997.

text.p: The share of imported cars in China's markets has fallen to its lowest level since the 1949 communist takeover, but imports could revive next year as domestic sales improve, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Imports have been hit by lower demand, high tariffs and growing domestic production with the market at 14 percent last year and expected to fall further this year, it said.
Market share averaged 48 percent from 1991 to 1996, compared with 61 percent in the 1960s and 1970s and 82 percent in the 1950s, the newspaper said.

However, imports were expected to rise again next year with the government expected to dismantle some tariff and non-tariff barriers as part of a bid to win entry to the World Trade Organisation, it said.

China imported about 110,000 cars in 1985, and that rose to 180,000 in 1993 and 170,000 in 1994, it quoted Chen Ping, vice president of the China Trading Centre of Imported Automobiles, China's largest distributor, as saying.
